one_liner: Netlify has a broad REST API with OAuth2 and self-serve personal access tokens. The pages don't confirm free-plan terms, and they don't confirm a vendor-run MCP server.
auth_notes: Personal access tokens are generated in user settings and sent as a Bearer token. Public integrations must use OAuth2, with an app registered in user settings. The OAuth2 authorization endpoint is https://app.netlify.com/authorize.
access_notes: Anyone with a Netlify account can generate a PAT or register an OAuth app. The pages say nothing about pricing or free-plan limits, so self_serve_free is inferred and low confidence. The partner pages cover revenue-share and deploy-partner programs. The docs state that you don't have to be a partner to build against the API.
blocker_notes: No blocker appears in the pages. Free-plan limits could not be verified from them. The deploy rate limits are 3 deploys per minute and 100 per day.

evidence.quote: If you’re making a public integration with Netlify for others to enjoy, you must use OAuth2.
Use your PAT for manual authentication in shell scripts or commands that use the Netlify API.
You can register a new application in your Netlify user settings for [OAuth applications](https://app.netlify.com/applications).

Use the Netlify REST API to manage atomic deploys of your sites and apps, manage form submissions, inject JavaScript snippets, manage DNS, and so much more.
You can browse the [OpenAPI reference for the Netlify API](https://open-api.netlify.com) to explore available endpoints.
